claim: Using single-cell RNA-seq, prohemocytes, monocytic hemocytes, and granulocytes were identified as the three major cell-types in the white shrimp hemolymph.
source: Using single-cell RNA-seq, we identified prohemocytes, monocytic hemocytes, and granulocytes as the three major cell-types in the white shrimp hemolymph.
evidence: The claim is directly supported by experimental data from single-cell RNA sequencing analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: A novel macrophage-like subset called monocytic hemocytes 2 (MH2) was identified, defined by the expression of certain marker genes, including Nlrp3 and Casp1.
source: Our results identified a novel macrophage-like subset called monocytic hemocytes 2 (MH2) defined by the expression of certain marker genes, including Nlrp3 and Casp1.
evidence: The identification is based on scRNA-seq data showing specific marker gene expression patterns.

claim: MH2 hemocytes are phagocytic.
source: This subtype of shrimp hemocytes is phagocytic and expresses markers that indicate some conservation with mammalian macrophages.
evidence: Supported by experimental phagocytosis assays using FITC-labeled bacteria.

claim: MH2 hemocytes express markers that indicate some conservation with mammalian macrophages.
source: This subtype of shrimp hemocytes is phagocytic and expresses markers that indicate some conservation with mammalian macrophages.
evidence: Based on comparative analysis of marker genes between shrimp MH2 cells and human macrophages.

claim: Invertebrates do not have B- and T-cell-based adaptive immunity.
source: Compared with vertebrates, invertebrates do not have B- and T-cell-based adaptive immunity, which makes them primarily reliant on innate immunity as defense against various pathogens (Little et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation to Little et al., 2005.

claim: Invertebrates are primarily reliant on innate immunity as defense against various pathogens.
source: Compared with vertebrates, invertebrates do not have B- and T-cell-based adaptive immunity, which makes them primarily reliant on innate immunity as defense against various pathogens (Little et al., 2005).
evidence: This follows logically from the lack of adaptive immunity and is supported by citation.

claim: Innate immune cells in invertebrates have 'trained immunity'.
source: Although invertebrates have developed diverse forms of innate immunity in order to adapt to various environmental challenges, the innate immune cells themselves contribute significantly because they have 'trained immunity' (Lanz-Mendoza and Contreras-Garduño, 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lanz-Mendoza and Contreras-Garduño, 2022.

claim: The evolution of innate immune systems has diverged into many branches in the metazoan tree of life.
source: However, the evolution of innate immune systems has diverged into many branches in the metazoan tree of life, making invertebrate immune cell-typing extremely complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on established evolutionary biology knowledge.

claim: The cells of the vertebrate immune system are conserved from chordates.
source: In contrast, the cells of the vertebrate immune system are conserved from chordates (Rosental et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rosental et al., 2018.

claim: Mosquito hemocytes are of four major types: prohemocytes, granulocytes, oenocytoids, and megacytes.
source: For example, recent research in mosquito cellular immunity revealed that mosquito hemocytes are of four major types (prohemocytes, granulocytes, oenocytoids, and megacytes) (Kwon et al., 2021; Raddi et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kwon et al., 2021 and Raddi et al., 2020.

claim: Drosophila melanogaster hemocytes can be divided into eight subgroups, including crystal cells, lamellocytes, unspecified plasmatocytes, proliferative plasmatocytes, PSC-like hemocytes, antimicrobial plasmatocytes, phagocytic plasmatocytes, and secretory plasmatocytes.
source: Hemocytes from another invertebrate model — Drosophila melanogaster — can be divided into eight subgroups, including crystal cells, lamellocytes, unspecified plasmatocytes, proliferative plasmatocytes, PSC-like hemocytes, antimicrobial plasmatocytes, phagocytic plasmatocytes, and secretory plasmatocytes (Cattenoz et al., 2021; Cho et al., 2020; Li et al., 2022; Tattikota et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to Cattenoz et al., 2021; Cho et al., 2020; Li et al., 2022; Tattikota et al., 2020.

claim: Penaeus vannamei is a popular mariculture species due to being fast growing and delectable.
source: This species was selected because it is a popular mariculture species due to being fast growing and delectable (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2019.

claim: Penaeus vannamei has an open circulatory system filled with hemolymph, which consists of plasma and hemocytes.
source: Additionally, this invertebrate has an open circulatory system filled with hemolymph, which consists of plasma and hemocytes (Lin and Söderhäll, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lin and Söderhäll, 2011.

claim: Shrimp hemolymph bears high similarity to vertebrate peripheral blood in terms of functions such as transportation of nutrients and metabolic waste, maintenance of acid–base equilibrium, defense against various invading pathogens, and hemostatic effect.
source: The shrimp hemolymph bears high similarity to that of the vertebrate peripheral blood in terms of functions such as transportation of nutrients and metabolic waste, maintenance of acid–base equilibrium, defense against various invading pathogens, and hemostatic effect (McNamara and Faria, 2012; Tassanakajon et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to McNamara and Faria, 2012 and Tassanakajon et al., 2018.

claim: The circulating plasma of shrimp contains more than 400 proteins, many of which are vertebrate homologs.
source: Moreover, the circulating plasma contains more than 400 proteins, many of which are vertebrate homologs (Luo et al., 2022; Tao et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Luo et al., 2022 and Tao et al., 2019.

claim: The circulating hemocytes of shrimp comprise proliferating cells, phagocytic cells, and effector secreting cells.
source: The circulating hemocytes comprise proliferating cells, phagocytic cells, and effector secreting cells (Lin and Söderhäll, 2011), which are functionally similar to vertebrate peripheral myeloid cells.
evidence: Supported by citation to Lin and Söderhäll, 2011.

claim: Shrimp circulating hemocytes are functionally similar to vertebrate peripheral myeloid cells.
source: The circulating hemocytes comprise proliferating cells, phagocytic cells, and effector secreting cells (Lin and Söderhäll, 2011), which are functionally similar to vertebrate peripheral myeloid cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional similarities described.

claim: Phagocytes have been identified in all metazoans.
source: Among these cells, the phagocytes have been identified in all metazoans (Musser et al., 2021), although they appear to be different in invertebrates and vertebrates.
evidence: Supported by citation to Musser et al., 2021.

claim: Bacterial engulfment in phagocytes may be conserved from invertebrates to vertebrates.
source: Some recently performed functional assays suggest that the bacterial engulfment in phagocytes may be conserved from invertebrates to vertebrates (Kokhanyuk et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kokhanyuk et al., 2021.

claim: Recombinant CREG (rCREG) was more effective than recombinant EGFP (rEGFP) in activating shrimp hemocytes.
source: Previously, we identified a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced shrimp plasma protein CREG and noticed that recombinant CREG (rCREG) was more effective than recombinant EGFP (rEGFP) in activating the shrimp hemocytes (Huang, Yang, & Wang, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by Huang, Yang, & Wang, 2021.

claim: A total of 34,693 cells including control (12544), rEGFP- (12640), and rCREG-treated (9509) cells were retained for analyses.
source: A total of 34,693 cells including control (12544), rEGFP- (12640), and rCREG-treated (9509) cells were retained for further analyses, and these cells exhibited a median of 5656, 6837, and 7916 transcripts and 1089.5, 1245, and 1364 genes per cell, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is direct experimental data from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: Control cells exhibited a median of 5656 transcripts and 1089.5 genes per cell.
source: A total of 34,693 cells including control (12544), rEGFP- (12640), and rCREG-treated (9509) cells were retained for further analyses, and these cells exhibited a median of 5656, 6837, and 7916 transcripts and 1089.5, 1245, and 1364 genes per cell, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is direct experimental data from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: rEGFP-treated cells exhibited a median of 6837 transcripts and 1245 genes per cell.
source: A total of 34,693 cells including control (12544), rEGFP- (12640), and rCREG-treated (9509) cells were retained for further analyses, and these cells exhibited a median of 5656, 6837, and 7916 transcripts and 1089.5, 1245, and 1364 genes per cell, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is direct experimental data from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: rCREG-treated cells exhibited a median of 7916 transcripts and 1364 genes per cell.
source: A total of 34,693 cells including control (12544), rEGFP- (12640), and rCREG-treated (9509) cells were retained for further analyses, and these cells exhibited a median of 5656, 6837, and 7916 transcripts and 1089.5, 1245, and 1364 genes per cell, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is direct experimental data from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: The rCREG-treated samples had the highest unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) and detected genes compared with the other two groups.
source: The rCREG-treated samples had the highest unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) and detected genes compared with that of the other two groups.
evidence: This is based on direct comparison of experimental data.

claim: CREG is a hemocyte activation factor.
source: This observation is consistent with our previous conclusion that CREG is a hemocyte activation factor (Huang et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work and current experimental observations.

claim: Five major groups of isolated hemocytes were identified: prohemocytes (PHs) (6838, 19.7%), granulocytes (GHs) (13871, 40%), monocytic hemocytes (MHs) (11112, 32%), transitional cells (TCs) (2090, 6%), and germ-like cells (GCs) (782, 2.3%).
source: We then aggregated the cell clusters and identified five major groups of isolated hemocytes, including prohemocytes (PHs) (6838, 19.7%), granulocytes (GHs) (13871, 40%), monocytic hemocytes (MHs) (11112, 32%), transitional cells (TCs) (2090, 6%), and germ-like cells (GCs) (782, 2.3%), which were annotated according to their potential functions implied by the marker genes (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is direct experimental data from scRNA-seq clustering analysis.

claim: Granulocytes are characterized by their ProPO system.
source: Granulocytes are characterized by their ProPO system (Sun et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sun et al., 2020.

claim: Prophenoloxidase activating factors 1 and 2 (PPAF1 and PPAF2) were highly expressed in the granulocyte population.
source: Here, we found that prophenoloxidase activating factors 1 and 2 (PPAF1 and PPAF2) were highly expressed in this population.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from scRNA-seq.

claim: Secreted proteins, including crustin-like protein (CRUL), penaeidin 3 a.1 (PEN-3), and crustacean hematopoietic factor-like protein (CHF), were highly expressed in the granulocyte population.
source: In addition to ProPO system genes, secreted proteins, including crustin-like protein (CRUL), penaeidin 3 a.1 (PEN-3), and crustacean hematopoietic factor-like protein (CHF), were also highly expressed in this population (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from scRNA-seq.

claim: Monocytic hemocytes share some critical genes with mammalian monocytes.
source: The MHs were named thus because they shared some critical genes with mammalian monocytes.
evidence: This is based on comparative gene expression analysis.

claim: NOD-like receptor protein 3 (Nlrp3) is a key component of the inflammasome and is highly expressed in monocytes and macrophages for processing of IL-1ß.
source: For example, NOD-like receptor protein 3 (Nlrp3) is a key component of the inflammasome and is highly expressed in monocytes and macrophages for processing of IL-1ß (He et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to He et al., 2016.

claim: Lysosome (Lyz1) is a well-known macrophage-secreting hydrolase.
source: Lysosome (Lyz1), another canonical antibacterial enzyme, is a well-known macrophage-secreting hydrolase (Short et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citation to Short et al., 1996.

claim: Vago5 encodes an IFN-like antiviral cytokine and plays a role in the anti-white spot syndrome virus (WSSV) resistance.
source: Vago5 encodes an IFN-like antiviral cytokine and plays a role in the anti-white spot syndrome virus (WSSV) resistance (C. Li, Yang, Hong, Zhao, & Wang, 2021) (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by citation to C. Li, Yang, Hong, Zhao, & Wang, 2021.

claim: Histone1 (h1f0) is the key component of heterochromatin assembly, and its high expression is associated with reduced gene expression and cell stemness properties.
source: In PHs, histone1 (h1f0) is the key component of heterochromatin assembly, and its high expression is associated with reduced gene expression and cell stemness properties (Pan and Fan, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pan and Fan, 2016.

claim: Hemocyte transglutaminase (TGM1) was identified as an immature hemocyte marker.
source: In a previous study, hemocyte transglutaminase (TGM1) was identified as an immature hemocyte marker (Koiwai et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Koiwai et al., 2021.

claim: The gene Igfbp7 has been shown to promote hemocyte proliferation in the small abalone Haliotis diversicolor.
source: The gene Igfbp7 has been shown to promote hemocyte proliferation in the small abalone Haliotis diversicolor (Wang et al., 2015; Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2015.

claim: Recombinant protein injection slightly increased the proportion of GHs and PHs and decreased the ratio of MHs.
source: Recombinant protein injection slightly increased the proportion of GHs and PHs and decreased the ratio of MHs (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cell type proportions from experimental data.

claim: There were no significant differences between the rEGFP and rCREG treatments in cell type proportions.
source: However, there were no significant differences between the rEGFP and rCREG treatments, which suggests that CREG is probably an activation factor rather than a differentiation factor for shrimp hemocytes.
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: CREG is probably an activation factor rather than a differentiation factor for shrimp hemocytes.
source: However, there were no significant differences between the rEGFP and rCREG treatments, which suggests that CREG is probably an activation factor rather than a differentiation factor for shrimp hemocytes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of significant differences in cell type proportions between treatments.

claim: Each major class type of hemocytes (PHs, MHs, and GHs) was divided into two subtypes and labelled PH1 (1577, 4.5%) and PH2 (5261, 15.2%), MH1 (10463, 30.2%) and MH2 (649, 1.9%), and GH1 (10353, 29.8%) and GH2 (3518, 10.1%), respectively.
source: To further trace the immune cell lineages in shrimp hemolymph, we subtyped the remaining three major classes of cells—PHs, MHs, and GHs; each major class type was divided into two subtypes and labelled PH1 (1577, 4.5%) and PH2 (5261, 15.2%), MH1 (10463, 30.2%) and MH2 (649, 1.9%), and GH1 (10353, 29.8%) and GH2 (3518, 10.1%), respectively (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on further clustering analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claim: Unique marker genes were identified for the subpopulations PH1, GH2, and MH2.
source: We identified some unique marker genes located at the edge of the t-SNE map for the subpopulations PH1, GH2, and MH2 (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 3, Supplementary file 4 and Supplementary file 5), but could not identify exclusive marker genes for the subpopulations PH2, GH1, and MH1, which constituted the main body of the t-SNE map.
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: Exclusive marker genes could not be identified for the subpopulations PH2, GH1, and MH1.
source: We identified some unique marker genes located at the edge of the t-SNE map for the subpopulations PH1, GH2, and MH2 (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 3, Supplementary file 4 and Supplementary file 5), but could not identify exclusive marker genes for the subpopulations PH2, GH1, and MH1, which constituted the main body of the t-SNE map.
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: The marker genes for PH2, GH1, and MH1 were also highly expressed in PH1, GH2, and MH2, respectively.
source: The marker genes for PH2, GH1, and MH1 were also highly expressed in PH1, GH2, and MH2, respectively (Figure 2B, Supplementary file 6, Supplementary file 7 and Supplementary file 8).
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: PH1 was characterized by high expression of all marker genes for the G1, G2, and M stages of the cell cycle.
source: To explore this, we performed cell cycle analyses of the six subtypes of hemocytes. PH1 was characterized by high expression of all marker genes for the G1, G2, and M stages (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on cell cycle gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: Approximately 2–5% of circulating hemocytes are proliferating hemocytes and can be labelled with BrdU.
source: This observation was consistent with a previous report that approximately 2–5% of circulating hemocytes were proliferating hemocytes and could be labelled with BrdU (Sun et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sun et al., 2013.

claim: Two major branches—MH lineage and GH lineage—were identified to have differentiated from one common PH.
source: Thus, we set PH1 as the initiating cell and applied a Monocle to construct differentiation trajectories for PHs, GHs, and MHs. Two major branches—MH lineage and GH lineage—were identified to have differentiated from one common PH (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: This is based on trajectory analysis using Monocle on scRNA-seq data.

claim: Shrimp hemocyte differentiation is similar to the development of human myeloid cells, in which granulocyte–monocyte progenitor (GMP) differentiates into monocyte and granulocyte.
source: This is similar to the development of human myeloid cells, in which granulocyte–monocyte progenitor (GMP) differentiates into monocyte and granulocyte (Bassler et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a comparative inference supported by citation to Bassler et al., 2019.

claim: Three shrimp homologs of human transcription factors (Fli1, MAF, and c-Rel) were identified among differentially expressed genes.
source: In total, 3790 differentially expressed genes among different branches were identified and are shown as a specific heatmap on which three shrimp homologs of human TFs were labeled (Figure 2F, Supplementary file 9).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis and homology comparison.

claim: Fli1 is specifically expressed in the granulocyte lineage.
source: Fli1 is specifically expressed in the granulocyte lineage, which is consistent with previous observations that Fli1 deletion decreases granulocytic cell number in mice (Starck et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data and supported by citation to Starck et al., 2010.

claim: Fli1 deletion decreases granulocytic cell number in mice.
source: Fli1 is specifically expressed in the granulocyte lineage, which is consistent with previous observations that Fli1 deletion decreases granulocytic cell number in mice (Starck et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Starck et al., 2010.

claim: MAF and c-Rel were highly expressed in the MH lineage.
source: MAF and c-Rel were highly expressed in the MH lineage (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from scRNA-seq.

claim: c-Rel is a key TF in the NF-κB pathway and plays important roles in monocyte differentiation.
source: c-Rel is a key TF in the NF-κB pathway and plays important roles in monocyte differentiation (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2020.

claim: MAF is a bZip TF that could induce monocytic differentiation.
source: MAF is a bZip TF that could induce monocytic differentiation (Kelly et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kelly et al., 2000.

claim: Some myeloid regulators may be conserved between shrimp and humans.
source: In general, our data suggest that some myeloid regulators may be conserved between shrimp and humans.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparative analysis of transcription factors.

claim: Nine MH2 marker genes have human homologs including chitotriosidase (CHIT1), lysozyme (Lyz1), lipase (LIPF), legumain (LGMN), Nlrp3, alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase (NAGA), zinc finger E-box-binding homeobox 1(zfh1), caspase1 (Casp1), and NPC intracellular cholesterol transporter 2 (NPC2).
source: We compared MH2 marker genes with that in the human database and found human homologs for nine MH2 marker genes including chitotriosidase (CHIT1), lysozyme (Lyz1), lipase (LIPF), legumain (LGMN), Nlrp3, alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase (NAGA), zinc finger E-box-binding homeobox 1(zfh1), caspase1 (Casp1), and NPC intracellular cholesterol transporter 2 (NPC2).
evidence: This is based on comparative genomic analysis using the Human Cell Atlas database.

claim: MH2 marker gene homologs are specifically expressed in human macrophages, including in some tissue-specific macrophages such as Kupffer cells and Hofbauer cells.
source: These genes were specifically expressed in human macrophages, including in some tissue-specific macrophages such as Kupffer cells and Hofbauer cells (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B; Karlsson et al., 2021).
evidence: This is based on comparison with Human Cell Atlas data, supported by citation to Karlsson et al., 2021.

claim: MH2 might be the invertebrate homolog of human macrophages.
source: This suggests that MH2 might be the invertebrate homolog of human macrophages, and various tissue-specific macrophages could have evolved from a common primitive cell type.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparative gene expression analysis.

claim: Various tissue-specific macrophages could have evolved from a common primitive cell type.
source: This suggests that MH2 might be the invertebrate homolog of human macrophages, and various tissue-specific macrophages could have evolved from a common primitive cell type.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the comparative analysis.

claim: Phagocytic hemocytes (R1) had round nuclei with a highly vacuolated cytoplasm similar to that in vertebrate macrophages.
source: To characterize these phagocytes, we observed them using confocal microscopy. These cells had round nuclei with a highly vacuolated cytoplasm similar to that in vertebrate macrophages (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on morphological observation using confocal microscopy.

claim: Cytochalasin D effectively suppressed the shrimp hemocyte phagocytosis rate.
source: To further compare these cells with vertebrate macrophage, we performed a phagocytosis inhibition assay using an actin polymerization inhibitor—cytochalasin D (Kokhanyuk et al., 2021)—that effectively suppressed the shrimp hemocyte phagocytosis rate (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is based on experimental phagocytosis inhibition assay data.

claim: CHIT1, Lyz1, and NAGA were expressed at higher levels in R1 (phagocytic hemocytes) than in R2 (control hemocytes).
source: To characterize the R1 cells, we quantified CHIT1, Lyz1, and NAGA expression in R1 and R2 using qPCR. The results indicated that these three genes were expressed at higher levels in R1 than in R2 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is based on qPCR experimental data.

claim: LYZ1, NAGA, and NLRP3 proteins were expressed at significantly higher levels in R1 (phagocytic hemocytes) than in R2 (control hemocytes).
source: In addition, we examined LYZ1, NAGA, and NLRP3 using immunoblotting and found that these three proteins were expressed at significantly higher levels in R1 than in R2 (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is based on immunoblotting experimental data.

claim: Phagocytic cells in shrimp hemolymph specifically expressed MH2 marker genes.
source: Thus, our results indicated that phagocytic cells in shrimp hemolymph specifically expressed MH2 marker genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on qPCR and immunoblotting data.

claim: MH2 may be an invertebrate homolog of human macrophages.
source: Our data suggest that MH2 may be an invertebrate homolog of human macrophages.
evidence: This is an inference based on multiple lines of evidence including gene expression, morphology, and functional assays.

claim: Shrimp hemocytes have been divided into three major types: hyalinocytes, semi-granulocytes, and granulocytes based on morphological criteria and functional properties.
source: Previously, shrimp hemocytes have been divided into three major types: hyalinocytes, semi-granulocytes, and granulocytes based on morphological criteria and functional properties (Söderhäll, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Söderhäll, 2016.

claim: Hyalinocyte marker genes were highly expressed in PH1, PH2, MH1, and MH2 groups.
source: Hyalinocyte marker genes were highly expressed in PH1, PH2, MH1, and MH2 groups (Figure 4A and D).
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: Semi-granulocyte marker genes were highly expressed in GH2 and MH2 groups.
source: Semi-granulocyte marker genes were highly expressed in GH2 and MH2 groups (Figure 4B and D).
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: Hyalinocytes contain both proliferating progenitors and phagocytic cells.
source: These data are consistent with previous observations that hyalinocytes contain both proliferating progenitors and phagocytic cells (Söderhäll, 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on current data and supported by citation to Söderhäll, 2016.

claim: Semi-granulocytes have phagocytic activities in some studies.
source: It also explained the observation of phagocytic activities in semi-granulocytes in some studies (Sun et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an inference based on current data and supported by citation to Sun et al., 2020.

claim: The granulocyte marker genes were highly expressed in GH2.
source: The granulocyte marker genes were consistent with our observations and were highly expressed in GH2 (Figure 4C–D), which indicates that granulocytes are indeed the largest cell-type with internal condensed granules (Söderhäll, 2016).
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: Granulocytes are the largest cell-type with internal condensed granules.
source: The granulocyte marker genes were consistent with our observations and were highly expressed in GH2 (Figure 4C–D), which indicates that granulocytes are indeed the largest cell-type with internal condensed granules (Söderhäll, 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression data and supported by citation to Söderhäll, 2016.

claim: Nlrp3 and Casp1 are two well-known mammalian macrophage inflammasome components.
source: Additionally, Nlrp3 and Casp1, two well-known mammalian macrophage inflammasome components were identified in these cells, suggesting that inflammasome-mediated anti-pathogenic processes might exist in invertebrate innate immunity and play a role in microbial restriction (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammalian macrophages.

claim: Inflammasome-mediated anti-pathogenic processes might exist in invertebrate innate immunity and play a role in microbial restriction.
source: Additionally, Nlrp3 and Casp1, two well-known mammalian macrophage inflammasome components were identified in these cells, suggesting that inflammasome-mediated anti-pathogenic processes might exist in invertebrate innate immunity and play a role in microbial restriction (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the presence of inflammasome components in shrimp cells, supported by citation to Wang et al., 2021.

claim: NAGA could inhibit macrophage activation via deglycosylation of macrophage activators.
source: NAGA, another enzyme found in macrophages, could inhibit macrophage activation via deglycosylation of macrophage activators (Saburi et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Saburi et al., 2017.

claim: The existence of NAGA in shrimp phagocytes implies that this subset of cells might share similar negative regulatory mechanisms recently partially uncovered in vertebrate macrophages.
source: The existence of NAGA in shrimp phagocytes implies that this subset of cells might share similar negative regulatory mechanisms recently partially uncovered in vertebrate macrophages (Luo et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the presence of NAGA, supported by citation to Luo et al., 2022.

claim: VEGF3 is a well-known angiogenic factor.
source: In addition, VEGF3, a well-known angiogenic factor, was also identified in this subtype (Eswarappa and Fox, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Eswarappa and Fox, 2015.

claim: In the primitive oyster Crassostrea gigas, approximately 40–60% of hemocytes engulf pathogens.
source: For example, in the primitive oyster Crassostrea gigas, approximately 40–60% of hemocytes engulf pathogens (Sun et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sun et al., 2021.

claim: In fish, most immune cells, including monocytes, granulocytes, B cells, and red blood cells, possess phagocytic activity against invading pathogens.
source: In fish, most immune cells, including monocytes, granulocytes, B cells, and red blood cells, possess phagocytic activity against invading pathogens (Heimroth et al., 2021; Li et al., 2006; Xu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Heimroth et al., 2021; Li et al., 2006; Xu et al., 2021.

claim: In humans, most myeloid cells, including monocytes, macrophages, dendritic cells, and neutrophils, engulf pathogens.
source: In humans, most myeloid cells, including monocytes, macrophages, dendritic cells, and neutrophils, engulf pathogens (Bassler et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bassler et al., 2019.

claim: Shrimps contain fewer phagocytes than other species.
source: Shrimps contain fewer phagocytes than do other species (Alenton et al., 2019; Huang et al., 2021; Li et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Alenton et al., 2019; Huang et al., 2021; Li et al., 2021.

claim: At least a part of the phagocytes in the shrimp hemolymph originated from a macrophage-like subset.
source: Our data suggest that at least a part of the phagocytes in the shrimp hemolymph originated from a macrophage-like subset.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing MH2 cells are phagocytic.

claim: Vertebrate macrophages include large populations of cells that reside in different tissues with diversified roles.
source: Moreover, vertebrate macrophages include large populations of cells that reside in different tissues with diversified roles.
evidence: This is established knowledge about vertebrate macrophages.

claim: Crustacean hyalinocytes are generally regarded as small phagocytes with few granules.
source: For example, crustacean hyalinocytes are generally regarded as small phagocytes with few granules (Lin and Söderhäll, 2011), but some researchers believe that these cells may be immature or prematurely released prohemocytes of the semi-granulocyte or granulocyte lineage (van de Braak et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Lin and Söderhäll, 2011.

claim: Some researchers believe that hyalinocytes may be immature or prematurely released prohemocytes of the semi-granulocyte or granulocyte lineage.
source: For example, crustacean hyalinocytes are generally regarded as small phagocytes with few granules (Lin and Söderhäll, 2011), but some researchers believe that these cells may be immature or prematurely released prohemocytes of the semi-granulocyte or granulocyte lineage (van de Braak et al., 2002).
evidence: This is an alternative interpretation supported by citation to van de Braak et al., 2002.

claim: The small cells in shrimp hemolymph include both prohemocytes and phagocytic hemocytes, and these two subtypes of cells have different marker genes and varied functional roles.
source: In this study, our data clearly indicated that the small cells though similar in morphology include both prohemocytes and phagocytic hemocytes, and these two subtypes of cells have different marker genes and varied functional roles in the shrimp hemolymph.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on scRNA-seq data showing distinct marker genes for different cell types.

claim: The terminally differentiated cells of the monocytic hemocyte lineage share several functional genes with mammalian macrophages.
source: The terminally differentiated cells of this lineage share several functional genes with mammalian macrophages, which suggests that this monocytic hemocyte lineage might be an invertebrate evolutionary homolog of the vertebrate monocyte lineage.
evidence: This is based on comparative gene expression analysis.

claim: Canonical correlation analysis was applied to perform batch correction on the combined cells from different treatments.

evidence: This is a description of the bioinformatics method used, supported by citation to Stuart et al., 2019.
